findings.narrative: According to City A.M., John Mountain succeeded Anne Boden as CEO in May 2023, not 30 June 2023 as claimed. City A.M. also reported that Boden's exit followed a clash with investors over fund manager Jupiter's decision to sell its stake at a below-valuation price the prior year. The quoted evidence does not address whether Boden remained on the board as a non-executive director or whether Mountain served in an interim capacity.

findings.narrative: The FCA fined Starling Bank Limited £28,959,426 for financial crime failings related to its financial sanctions screening, according to the FCA. Per the FCA, the penalty would have been £40,959,426, but Starling qualified for a 30% discount after agreeing to resolve the matters; Reuters similarly reports the discount resulted from cooperation with the regulator. The quoted evidence does not confirm the 27 September 2024 date or that the action took the form of a Final Notice, so those elements of the claim remain unverified.

evidence.quote: Britain's financial watchdog has fined Starling Bank 29 million pounds ($38.5 million) after finding the digital lender's anti-money laundering controls and sanctions screening systems left the financial system "wide open to criminals".

findings.narrative: The FCA fined Starling Bank Limited £28,959,426 for financial crime failings related to its financial sanctions screening, and found the bank repeatedly breached a requirement not to open accounts for high-risk customers (fca.org.uk). Reuters reported the fine as £29 million ($38.5 million), stating the watchdog found the digital lender's anti-money laundering controls and sanctions screening systems left the financial system "wide open to criminals." Neither quoted source specifies a September 2024 payment date, so that element of the claim is not confirmed by the evidence provided.
